CVE-2026-123829.title: Node.js is vulnerable to Permission Model file-name disclosure via recursive fs.watch
CVE-2026-123829.description: A Permission Model bypass in Node.js recursive file watching discloses the names of files and directories the process is not permitted to read. On macOS and Windows, fs.watch() and fs.promises.watch() in recursive mode are backed by the native libuv watcher: FSEventWrap::Start checks kFileSystemRead only once, on the watched root, and FSEventWrap::OnEvent then forwards every filename libuv reports (relative paths at any depth) to the JavaScript callback without checking that each path is covered by the read grant. Code running under --permission with an exact read grant on a directory can therefore learn names such as sub/secret.txt even though readdir on that subdirectory is denied. The flaw exposes names and timing metadata, not file contents, and requires macOS or Windows plus files created under the watched directory by another actor. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x.

CVE-2026-136500.title: SQL injection with BIG5 aliases and the JOHAB, EUC_TW, EUC_CN and EUC_KR client encodings
CVE-2026-136500.description:
To escape a bound parameter, or a name passed to a catalog function, psqlODBC has to know where each multibyte character of the client encoding ends. It treated a client encoding named by an alias the server accepts, such as WIN950, Windows950 or big-5 for BIG5, as single-byte, and it accepted too narrow a range of lead bytes for JOHAB, EUC_TW, EUC_CN and EUC_KR. A quote byte that the server reads as part of such a character was then not doubled, or a quote the server reads on its own was taken for part of a character, and the literal ended early.

An end user who controls one bound character parameter, or a name the application passes to a catalog function such as SQLTables(), can run SQL with the rights of the application's database role. This requires a connection that is not in UTF-8: the ANSI driver, or the ANSI entry points, with one of these client encodings. CVE-2026-62333.title: OpenVM: MemoryMerkleAir allows below-leaf rows to alter memory roots
CVE-2026-62333.description: OpenVM is a performant and modular zkVM framework built for customization and extensibility. Before 1.7.0 in the 1.x line and in affected 2.0 and 2.1 prereleases, `MemoryMerkleAir` does not forbid Merkle expansion rows at `parent_height` = 0 or below while `expand_direction` != 0. A malicious prover can fabricate a subtree below a memory leaf and swap digests inside that subtree to change the committed memory root without a corresponding memory operation. The fraudulent rows still balance against the Merkle and compression buses and require no memory-bus operation for the changed leaf. Because the memory Merkle root binds VM memory state across continuation segment boundaries, this affects the soundness of OpenVM proofs using persistent memory. This issue is fixed in versions 1.7.0, 2.0.0-rc.3 and 2.1.0-preview.

CVE-2026-99652.title: mm: fix deadlock of mremap() against UFFDIO_MOVE
CVE-2026-99652.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm: fix deadlock of mremap() against UFFDIO_MOVE

With per-VMA locks, UFFDIO_MOVE can run concurrently with mremap()
on different VMAs in the same mm. Those VMAs can share page tables, so
both operations can acquire the same pair of page-table locks.

UFFDIO_MOVE orders the locks by address, while mremap() takes the source
lock first. These conflicting orders can deadlock; mremap() holding
mmap_lock for writing no longer helps.

Move double_pt_lock() and double_pt_unlock() to mm/internal.h and use
them for all page-table moves in mremap(). Preserve the source entry
checks after acquiring both locks. Remove the comments claiming that
exclusive mmap_lock makes lock ordering irrelevant.

In move_ptes(), make sure to just recheck source and destination PMD
after taking the locks and drop the overly-long comment.

Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Chris Mason in private.
